material_definitions: The material series investigated are the lithium argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, systematically exploring the influence of aliovalent substitution.
The samples were characterized using X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance.
Increasing Ge content induces an anion site disorder and significantly drops the activation barrier for ionic motion.
The fastest resulting argyrodite composition achieved 5.4 mS cm-1 in a cold-pressed state and 18.4 mS cm-1 upon sintering.
The material series investigated are the lithium argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, systematically exploring the influence of aliovalent substitution.
The samples were characterized using X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance.
Increasing Ge content induces an anion site disorder and significantly drops the activation barrier for ionic motion.
The fastest resulting argyrodite composition achieved 5.4 mS cm-1 in a cold-pressed state and 18.4 mS cm-1 upon sintering.

Inspired by the possibility of incorporating Ge into a composition possessing a larger unit cell, we have investigated the effect of Ge4+ substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I on the structuretransport relationships.

Using a combination of Rietveld refinements against neutron and X-ray diffraction data, we identify the underlying structural changes associated with the Li- and anion-substructures including changes to the site-disorder.
With increasing Ge-fraction, the diffusion pathways for Li+ expand and site disorder between the S2– and I– positions appears.

The increasing disorder is correlated to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in the conductivity over orders of magnitude leading to the highest lithium argyrodites reported so far.

With increasing Ge-fraction, the diffusion pathways for Li+ expand and site disorder between the S2– and I– positions appears.

The increasing disorder is correlated to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in the conductivity over orders of magnitude leading to the highest lithium argyrodites reported so far.
Aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I was performed, investigating changes to structure and transport using diffraction, NMR, and impedance spectroscopy.
With increasing Ge content, significant changes in activation barrier were observed, coinciding with increasing I–/S2– site disorder and increasing lattice volume.
The structural changes lead to opening of the bottle necks and more facile inter-cage jumps.
The resulting material, Li6.6P0.4Ge0.6S5I, exhibited a high ionic conductivity.
Sintering of the pellets further increased the ionic conductivity up to 18.4 mS cm-1.

Solid solutions of the formula Li6+xP1-xGexS5I where x varies from 0 to 0.8.
These materials belong to the lithium argyrodite family.
The series involves substituting P5+ with Ge4+ and adding Li+ for charge balance.
The substitution affects the ionic conductivity and activation energy of the electrolyte.
